title: The Impact of Attachment and Parental Conflict on Children's Unconscious Attitudes and Behaviors

incidental_findings: Prolonged exposure to high-conflict environments contributes to long-term neurological changes, mentioned alongside behavioral outcomes but not elaborated as a primary focus
Insecure attachment increases sensitivity to perceived threats specifically, suggesting a calibration mechanism beyond general emotional dysregulation
technical_sidenotes: Early caregiver-child dynamics shape implicit cognitive structures — implying pre-verbal, non-declarative memory systems encode relational patterns that persist outside conscious awareness

The framing of 'internal working models' as implicit beliefs bridges attachment theory with cognitive neuroscience constructs like predictive coding, though the mechanism linking the two is not specified
Distorted social perception is listed as a distinct outcome from negative self-narratives, suggesting separable downstream pathways from insecure attachment — one interoceptive, one exteroceptive

title: Enteral feeding initiation and feeding practices in pediatric traumatic brain injury patients admitted to the neurotrauma intensive care unit.

unexplained_variances: Early feeding benefits were significant in mild TBI but NOT observed in moderate or severe TBI patients, despite severe TBI comprising the largest subgroup (44%) — this contradicts the general assumption that nutritional support would be most critical in the most severely injured patients.
Only 39% of patients reached 70% of caloric target within 7 days, suggesting a systemic failure in nutritional delivery that the study design did not fully explain.

The correlation between early feeding and reduced LOS was weak (r = 0.25 for NICU, r = 0.33 for hospital), yet the median LOS differences were large (5.5 vs 10 days), suggesting confounders or a nonlinear relationship not captured by the linear correlation.
Multivariate analysis showed neurosurgery — not feeding timing — influenced hospital LOS and discharge GCS, undermining the primary hypothesis that early feeding drives better outcomes.
incidental_findings: Planned surgical/radiological and airway procedures were the dominant cause of feeding interruption (59%), far exceeding physiological causes like feed intolerance (16.6%) or hemodynamic instability (9.9%) — suggesting iatrogenic delays are the primary barrier to early nutrition.

Feed refusal accounted for 14.6% of interruptions, an unexpectedly high rate in a pediatric population that presumably includes many patients too impaired to refuse — implying a subpopulation with preserved consciousness but behavioral feeding resistance.
17% in-hospital mortality rate reported without breakdown by feeding group, leaving open whether early feeding had any survival signal or whether mortality was entirely predicted by admission GCS.
technical_sidenotes: The differential response to early feeding by TBI severity (benefit in mild but not moderate/severe) suggests a possible threshold mechanism: neurological recovery in mild TBI may be metabolically gated, while moderate/severe TBI recovery is dominated by structural damage that nutrition alone cannot address.

The study was conducted in a lower-middle-income country setting, where baseline nutritional status and resource constraints may create a different physiological starting point — the 48-hour early feeding cutoff may interact with pre-existing malnutrition in ways not seen in high-income cohorts.

Admission GCS score predicted mortality in multivariate analysis but not discharge GCS or LOS, suggesting that the prognostic value of GCS is specific to survival rather than functional recovery — these may be governed by different physiological pathways.

title: A Discourse Analysis of Suicide Tendency in Photographer Lu Dawson’s Posts on Public Acconts: An Approach of Non-real World and Real World

unexplained_variances: Suicidal expression was more direct on the platform with more followers (Weibo), contradicting the intuitive expectation that people would be more guarded or indirect about suicidal ideation before a larger audience
incidental_findings: Platform audience size correlated with directness of suicidal language — the blogger used different disclosure strategies across Weibo (larger audience) vs. Xiaohongshu (smaller audience), suggesting platform context modulates self-disclosure of crisis states
Heavy use of 'vaguely restricted adverbs' (hedging language) co-occurred with otherwise direct suicidal expression, presenting a paradoxical mix of certainty and uncertainty in the same discourse
technical_sidenotes: The co-occurrence of first-person singular pronouns, negative lexicon, and rhetorical questions was described as 'highly consistent with symptoms of depression as defined by neurology,' implying a claimed but unexplored bridge between linguistic markers and neurological diagnostic criteria

The 'reality orientation' vs. 'non-reality orientation' discourse framework (Kugrerberg & Gliat, 2012) was applied to social media posts of a suicidal individual — the paper implies but does not fully elaborate how depression shifts discourse toward non-reality orientation

Apologetic sentence structures were highlighted as a syntactic marker of guilt, suggesting a potential computational linguistic feature for automated detection of depressive guilt distinct from general negative sentiment

title: A General Theory of Adaptivity and Homeostasis in the Brain and in the Body

unexplained_variances: LMS algorithm, traditionally a supervised learning method, can be reformulated to perform unsupervised learning — this contradicts the standard categorization of LMS as inherently requiring an external error signal
The combination of two fundamentally different learning paradigms (unsupervised Hebbian and supervised LMS) yields a functional hybrid, despite their theoretical incompatibility
incidental_findings: The authors suggest the Hebbian-LMS hybrid may describe the actual learning algorithm used by biological neural networks at the neuron and synapse level ('nature's little secret'), implying biological learning may incorporate error-correction mechanisms not typically associated with Hebbian plasticity
The hybrid algorithm is claimed to have 'practical engineering applications' beyond theoretical neuroscience, suggesting bidirectional utility between biological modeling and signal processing
technical_sidenotes: The existence of an unsupervised form of LMS implies that error signals for synaptic weight adjustment could be generated locally without an external teacher — a mechanism that, if biological, would resolve the 'credit assignment problem' debate in computational neuroscience

The framing of Hebbian learning as implementable via LMS suggests that correlation-based plasticity (Hebb) and error-minimization plasticity (LMS) may not be distinct biological mechanisms but two perspectives on the same underlying synaptic update rule

title: Unveiling complexity: non-linear and fractal analysis in neuroscience and cognitive psychology

unexplained_variances: The exact cognitive and neuronal variables that exhibit significant chaotic patterns remain an open question, despite the broad demonstrated applicability of nonlinear methods across neuroscience.

The relationship between 1/f scaling in neural and cognitive functions and metastability of brain states is described as potentially causal but not yet confirmed — the mechanism linking fractal temporal dynamics to metastable state transitions is unresolved.
incidental_findings: Fractal analysis proved useful not only for temporal neuronal dynamics but also for evaluating structural patterns of cellular organization in both normal and pathological histologic brain samples — an application beyond the expected domain of dynamical systems.

Nonlinear methods showed diagnostic utility for neurological and psychiatric disorders, including monitoring natural history and evaluating therapeutic effects — a clinical application that emerged secondary to the modeling focus.

Noise (1/f / pink noise) appears to be functionally pervasive across both neural and cognitive levels, suggesting it is not mere measurement artifact but a feature with possible causal significance for brain state dynamics.
technical_sidenotes: Cognitive functions can be successfully modeled via transient activity of large-scale brain networks in the presence of noise, implying noise is not disruptive but constitutive of information processing (Rabinovich et al., 2008).

The brain's phase space is described as having multiple equilibrium points, limit cycles, stability regions, and unstable periodic orbits with period-doubling bifurcations — suggesting the brain operates near bifurcation boundaries, which could explain rapid state transitions.

Strange attractors reframe higher cognitive functions (language, attention, memory, decision-making) as emergent systemic properties of parallel information streams between distributed, highly interconnected neuronal clusters modulated by central nodes — replacing localizationist models.

Self-organization accounts for evolutionary emergence of new complex cognitive structures from non-deterministic random patterns, drawing a direct parallel to nonlinear fluid dynamics (Dixon et al., 2012).

Decision-making can be represented by ODE-based dynamic models with finite possibilities at decision points and basic rules for uncertainty (Holmes et al., 2004) — a neuroeconomics finding bridging dynamical systems theory and behavioral choice.

title: Fat embolism syndrome and massive middle cerebral artery occlusion: a case report.

unexplained_variances: Symptoms started in the recovery ward, implying onset during or immediately after a procedure rather than the typical delayed onset of several hours to days post-trauma/reduction

A complete flow interruption by adipose material was observed in the left middle cerebral artery, which is a focal occlusion pattern rather than the diffuse pattern described as typical for FES neurological involvement
incidental_findings: The case demonstrates that fat embolism can cause large-vessel occlusion (left MCA), not just the expected microvascular/diffuse injury pattern, suggesting a mechanism more akin to thrombotic stroke than classical FES
technical_sidenotes: MRI pattern of neurological damage in FES changes according to timing, implying a dynamic pathophysiological process that evolves from initial insult
Complete arterial occlusion by adipose material in a major cerebral vessel challenges the conventional model that fat emboli are primarily a microvascular/capillary-level phenomenon

title: Management of medically unresponsive detrusor urethral dyssynergia in three dogs by perineal urethrostomy

unexplained_variances: Medical management (typically effective for detrusor-urethral dyssynergia) completely failed in all three cases, yet a purely anatomical/surgical intervention (perineal urethrostomy) immediately resolved the functional disorder — suggesting the pathophysiology may not be purely neurogenic smooth muscle dyscoordination as the 'idiopathic' label implies.

All three dogs urinated with a normal uninterrupted stream at their very first postoperative urination, indicating instantaneous resolution of a supposedly neuromuscular coordination disorder — an unexpectedly rapid response inconsistent with gradual neural adaptation or relearning.
incidental_findings: All three affected animals were male, raising an unaddressed question about whether urethral anatomy (longer, narrower urethra with os penis constriction) contributes to or is necessary for this syndrome to manifest — a sex-linked anatomical predisposition was not discussed.

No major postoperative complications were reported despite perineal urethrostomy being described as a 'salvage procedure,' suggesting the risk profile may be more favorable than framed, at least for this specific indication.

Long-term follow-up showed zero recurrence, which is notable because if the underlying detrusor-sphincter dyscoordination were truly central/neurogenic in origin, bypassing the distal urethra should not permanently resolve proximal sphincter dysfunction.
technical_sidenotes: The diagnosis was made entirely by exclusion (characteristic urination pattern + absence of structural/neurological abnormalities) rather than by direct urodynamic confirmation (e.g., simultaneous cystometry and sphincter EMG), leaving open the possibility that the actual mechanism was a fixed distal urethral obstruction undetectable by catheterization or imaging — a functional rather than anatomical stenosis.

The immediate surgical cure by urethrostomy (which bypasses the penile urethra and external urethral sphincter) implies the site of dyssynergia may be localized to the distal striated urethral sphincter or penile urethra specifically, rather than the proximal smooth muscle sphincter — a mechanistic distinction not explored by the authors.
Residual bladder volume was estimated by ultrasound rather than direct catheterization, introducing measurement uncertainty that could mask incomplete emptying.

title: Stroke Lesions as a Rosetta Stone for Language Model Interpretability

unexplained_variances: Mapping success was 67% for picture naming but 68.3% for sentence completion — the authors do not explain why sentence completion mapped slightly better despite picture naming being a more constrained task with less variability in expected outputs.

33% of picture naming conditions and 31.7% of sentence completion conditions failed to map above chance — the authors do not characterize what distinguished the failing conditions from the successful ones.

The final sentence explicitly flags that behavioral alignment may NOT reflect shared computational principles — the authors achieved strong statistical mapping but cannot confirm the underlying mechanisms are actually homologous.
incidental_findings: Semantic-dominant LLM errors mapped onto ventral-stream (temporal) lesion patterns while phonemic-dominant errors mapped onto dorsal-stream (frontoparietal) patterns — this dual dissociation in an artificial system was not the stated goal but recapitulates the classical dual-stream model of speech processing.

LLM error profiles were 'sufficiently similar' to human error profiles to be projectable into human lesion space at all — the fact that transformer perturbations produce error distributions that resemble aphasic error distributions is itself a striking secondary observation.
technical_sidenotes: The symptom-to-lesion direction is inverted from typical lesion-symptom mapping (which predicts deficits from lesion location) — they trained models to predict brain damage location FROM behavioral error profiles, enabling projection of LLM errors into anatomical space.

The framework relies on chronic post-stroke aphasia (N=410), meaning the brain data reflects reorganized/compensated neural states rather than acute damage — the mapping is to stabilized lesion-behavior relationships, not immediate perturbation effects.

Systematic perturbations were applied to transformer layers specifically, implying layer-level granularity was sufficient to produce clinically recognizable error profiles — the resolution at which LLM 'lesions' produce human-like deficits is itself a mechanistic finding.

title: Rethinking Learning: What the Interdisciplinary Science Tells Us

unexplained_variances: The authors claim 100 years of learning theory is 'woefully inadequate' but do not specify which empirical predictions failed or what measurable outcomes deviated from theoretical expectations — the variance is asserted rather than demonstrated with data.

No explanation is offered for why integrating neuroscience, anthropology, psychology, and education into a unified framework has not already been achieved despite decades of interdisciplinary research, suggesting unexplored institutional or epistemological barriers.
incidental_findings: The framing implies that 'deep learning' and 'equity' are coupled outcomes — suggesting the authors observed or assume that environments optimizing for one tend to produce the other, though this correlation is not empirically substantiated in the abstract.

The emphasis on 'embodied and coordinated through social interaction' as a distinct principle hints that prior cognitive-only models produced anomalous results when applied to socially situated or physically active learning contexts.
technical_sidenotes: Learning is described as 'rooted in evolutionary, biological, and neurological systems' — bundling three distinct levels of analysis (phylogenetic, ontogenetic, neural) into a single principle, which implies cross-level interactions the authors find noteworthy but do not decompose.

The integration of emotion, identity, and cognition as inseparable developmental processes challenges modular theories of mind and suggests the authors encountered evidence that affective and identity-related variables could not be cleanly separated from cognitive measures.

Reference to learning as 'embodied' points to grounded/embodied cognition literature where sensorimotor systems participate in knowledge representation — a mechanism still debated in neuroscience and flagged here as foundational rather than supplementary.

title: Is it time to rethink how we page physicians? Understanding paging patterns in a tertiary care hospital

unexplained_variances: The hypothesis that paging volumes follow consistent temporal trends regardless of service type was supported, but the authors could not explain WHY the patterns converge across fundamentally different medical and surgical services — the underlying causal mechanism remains unidentified.
1% of pages (approximately 258) are unaccounted for in the ER vs. inpatient breakdown (75% + 24% = 99%), suggesting a small category of pages from neither source that is not discussed.
incidental_findings: ER pages peaked earlier (16:30–20:00) than inpatient unit pages (17:30–18:30), suggesting distinct workflow drivers between these two settings despite converging on the same residents — the offset is noted but not explored.

The median inter-page interval of 22:30 minutes across all specialties implies residents are interrupted roughly every 22 minutes during active periods, a cadence the authors flag as relevant to burnout but do not correlate with error rates or cognitive load measures.

The remarkably low standard deviation (±12 pages/day on a mean of 211) suggests paging volume is highly predictable day-to-day, which is itself an unexplored finding with implications for staffing optimization.
technical_sidenotes: The late-afternoon paging surge (16:30–18:30) coincides with nursing shift changes and end-of-day order reconciliation, but the authors only identify this as an 'area for future study' without confirming the mechanism.

The study implicitly reveals that the paging system architecture (single primary pager per service) creates a bottleneck where all requests funnel to one resident — a systems-level design issue flagged as contributing to burnout but not further analyzed.

title: A disruptive cue improves handwashing in school children in Zambia.

unexplained_variances: Both intervention AND control schools saw an increase in handwashing without soap, suggesting a strong Hawthorne/observation effect that was not fully explained or controlled for.

The confidence interval for the soap-use odds ratio is extremely wide (1.76-29.71), indicating high variance across schools that the authors do not explain — some intervention schools likely showed little or no effect while others showed massive effects.
incidental_findings: The 'disruptive cue' mechanism was designed to interrupt habitual neurological patterns, yet the control group also changed behavior (handwashing without soap increased), suggesting that the study measurement process itself may have acted as a disruptive cue.

The participatory process to identify a 'locally appropriate' cue converged on soap-on-a-rope — implying that the physical accessibility/convenience of soap (not knowledge or motivation) was the binding constraint, which reframes the problem as logistical rather than psychological.
technical_sidenotes: The authors invoke 'habitual neurological patterns' as the target of disruption but do not measure or verify any neurological or habit-loop mechanism — the actual pathway (cue disruption vs. simple soap availability vs. novelty effect) remains unidentified.

The framing positions nudge theory as operating through environmental cue disruption of existing habits, but soap-on-a-rope simultaneously reduces friction (makes soap available at point of use) and introduces novelty — these are distinct behavioral mechanisms that are conflated.

The disconnect between knowledge and practice ('knowledge-action gap') is noted but the study does not measure whether the intervention changed knowledge, attitudes, or purely the motor/environmental pathway, leaving the mechanism of action unresolved.

title: ACTRIMS Forum 2021 – Poster Presentations

incidental_findings: Shiatsu accounted for 2.9% of referrals — an unconventional complementary therapy appearing alongside standard medical referrals (physiotherapy, neurology, psychiatry) without explanation of its clinical rationale or outcomes in MS rehabilitation.

Psychiatry referrals were notably low (0.3%) despite the known psychological burden of both MS and pandemic isolation, contrasting sharply with psychology referrals (21.4%) — the disparity is not discussed.

Art therapy and neurology referrals were identical (1% each), suggesting neurology consults were surprisingly infrequent for an MS-specific service during a period when disease management was reportedly disrupted.

title: A Case of 22q11 Deletion Syndrome (22q11DS) with a Panayiotopoulos Epileptic Pattern: Are Additional Copy-Number Variations a Possible Second Hit in Modulating the 22q11DS Phenotype?

unexplained_variances: Only 15.2% of 22q11DS patients develop epilepsy despite sharing the same deletion, and no candidate gene for epilepsy has been identified within the deleted region itself.

The 2q37 microduplication was inherited from the mother who never had seizures, meaning neither the 22q11.2 deletion nor the 2q37 duplication alone is sufficient to cause epilepsy — the phenotype only emerged from their co-occurrence.
The extreme variable expressivity and reduced penetrance of 22q11DS remain unexplained by the primary deletion alone, suggesting a multi-hit or oligogenic model.
incidental_findings: Array CGH revealed an unexpected additional 172 kb microduplication at 2q37 that was not part of the primary diagnostic finding, harboring three genes including DGKD.

The distal breakpoint of the 2q37 duplication directly interrupts the DGKD gene, mirroring a previously reported t(X;2) translocation disrupting DGKD in an unrelated epilepsy patient — a convergent structural hit on the same gene across independent cases.

Rare additional CNVs outside the 22q11.2 region have been shown to modulate risk of congenital heart defects in 22q11DS, and the authors propose this same modifier mechanism extends to the epileptic phenotype.
technical_sidenotes: DGKD encodes diacylglycerol kinase delta, a cytoplasmic enzyme that phosphorylates diacylglycerol to phosphatidic acid — a second messenger in a lipid signaling pathway independently implicated in epilepsy and other neurological diseases.

The epilepsy subtype was specifically classifiable as Panayiotopoulos syndrome, a benign childhood occipital epilepsy — an unusually specific and typically self-limiting form, raising the question of why this particular epilepsy subtype emerged from this genetic combination.

The two-hit model proposed (22q11.2 deletion + distant CNV modifier) suggests that background rare CNV burden may be a general mechanism for phenotypic variability across all 22q11DS manifestations, not just cardiac or epileptic.

title: Hearing Loss in Stroke Cases: A Literature Review

unexplained_variances: Hearing loss after stroke is described as 'very common' in stroke populations, yet it has not been as extensively investigated as visual deficits — the authors attribute this gap to the 'invisible' nature of hearing loss but acknowledge this explanation is speculative and insufficient given the prevalence data.

SCA infarction produces contralateral sensorineural hearing loss (because fibers have already crossed), yet PICA and AICA strokes produce mostly ipsilateral hearing loss with mixed cochlear/retrocochlear patterns — the laterality inversion across vascular territories is noted but not mechanistically reconciled.

Auditory-processing deficits after stroke are described as 'possibly under-documented,' implying observed prevalence may be significantly higher than reported, but no explanation is offered for why standard clinical assessments systematically miss them.
incidental_findings: A past history of stroke in the general population independently increases the likelihood of having hearing loss, suggesting a chronic or degenerative auditory effect beyond the acute event itself.
Auditory dysfunction may predict long-term patient outcome after stroke — mentioned as a secondary observation without elaboration on mechanism or effect size.

Hearing loss may restrict participation in rehabilitation programs and lead to inferior physical performance outcomes (Landi et al., 2006), framing hearing loss not just as a sensory deficit but as an independent predictor of functional recovery failure.
technical_sidenotes: Both hemorrhagic and ischemic strokes can interrupt 'all stages of the hearing path,' and hearing deficits can onset before, during, or shortly after the stroke event — the pre-stroke onset timing is flagged but unexplained, suggesting possible prodromal vascular compromise of the auditory pathway.

PICA and AICA territory strokes produce mixed cochlear/retrocochlear patterns, with less frequent retrocochlear-only patterns — the mixed presentation implies simultaneous peripheral and central auditory damage from a single vascular event.

Cortical or central deafness after stroke is described as 'even rarer' than vertebrobasilar hearing loss, implying bilateral cortical damage is required, which is an unusual stroke presentation worth mechanistic investigation.

title: Alcohol-Related Hospitalizations During the Initial COVID-19 Lockdown in Massachusetts: An Interrupted Time-Series Analysis.

unexplained_variances: Alcohol-related hospitalizations dropped 80% during lockdown (RR 0.20), far exceeding what reduced healthcare access alone would predict — the authors expected increased alcohol use during lockdown stress, not dramatically fewer hospitalizations

Post-lockdown alcohol-related hospitalizations recovered only to 72% of pre-lockdown rates (RR 0.72), not returning to baseline, suggesting a persistent structural or behavioral shift that the study does not explain

The parallel drop in all-cause hospitalizations complicates attribution — the alcohol-specific decline may be confounded by general healthcare avoidance rather than reflecting actual changes in alcohol consumption or harm
incidental_findings: All-cause hospitalizations followed the same temporal pattern as alcohol-related ones, suggesting the lockdown effect was not specific to alcohol but a system-wide phenomenon of reduced hospital utilization

The VA population (predominantly male veterans) showed this pattern, raising the unaddressed question of whether social isolation reduced triggers for alcohol-related crises (e.g., fewer social drinking contexts, bar closures, reduced interpersonal conflict) or merely suppressed help-seeking behavior

The study implicitly reveals that a large fraction of alcohol-related hospitalizations may be driven by contextual/environmental triggers rather than chronic addiction severity, since removal of social context produced such a dramatic reduction
technical_sidenotes: The use of ICD-10 primary diagnosis codes to define alcohol-related hospitalizations means cases where alcohol was a contributing but secondary factor would be missed, potentially masking a different pattern in alcohol-complicated admissions

The lockdown period was only ~10 weeks (March 10 – May 18, 2020), making the rate estimate of 10 per 100,000 patient-months based on a very small denominator — the 95% CI of 0.10-0.39 reflects this imprecision

Exclusion of observation-status patients may systematically exclude brief alcohol-related presentations (e.g., acute intoxication managed in ED/observation), potentially biasing toward more severe cases and obscuring trends in less severe alcohol-related healthcare encounters

title: Sound of a Slogan: Appealing to Audiences in the Global Market☆
Assessment of long-term psychosocial outcomes in N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor encephalitis – the SAPIENCE study protocol

unexplained_variances: Despite good functional neurological recovery, most patients continue to experience cognitive, psychiatric, psychological, and social impairments years after the acute phase — the disconnect between functional recovery and persistent deficits is noted but unexplained
The precise nature and evolving patterns over time of long-term consequences remain unclear, suggesting existing models of NMDAR encephalitis recovery do not account for observed chronic trajectories
incidental_findings: The study highlights that predominantly young patients are affected, implying an age-related susceptibility or impact pattern that is acknowledged but not explored mechanistically
Caregiver burden is included as a study focus, suggesting observed but under-documented psychosocial effects extending beyond the patient
technical_sidenotes: The framing implies that NMDAR autoantibody-mediated damage may produce lasting subclinical neurological changes not captured by standard functional assessments — a potential dissociation between macroscale recovery and microscale synaptic or network-level dysfunction

title: Application of Eye Tracking Technology in Medicine: A Bibliometric Analysis

unexplained_variances: Three distinct peaks in publication growth (2011, 2015, 2017) rather than smooth exponential growth — the authors do not explain what drove these specific surges or the apparent dip/plateau between them

Autism spectrum disorders dominated the field disproportionately (638 of 2456 articles, ~26%) despite psychiatry and neuroscience being broader categories — no explanation for why ASD captured such outsized research attention relative to other conditions
incidental_findings: ASD-specific publication growth rate (16.52%) substantially exceeded the overall field growth rate (11.14%), suggesting accelerating concentration of research into a single condition

The majority of ASD eye-tracking studies narrowly focused on social interaction gaze patterns, implying other potentially informative gaze behaviors (e.g., repetitive visual exploration, sensory processing, executive function tasks) are underexplored

Extensive three-country collaboration networks (USA, UK, Germany) dominated production, with the rest of the world collectively underrepresented — potential geographic bias in study populations and paradigms

title: Harrison's Neurology in Clinical Medicine. First Edition.

incidental_findings: The book pursues 'numerous, smaller divergences in neurology' not found in Harrison's Internal Medicine, including prion disease, effects of HIV on the nervous system, auto-immune diseases of the nervous system, and uncommon cancers of the nervous system.
technical_sidenotes: The reviewer, an academic neuroscience researcher, noted 'interesting clinical insights into disorders caused by molecular processes,' suggesting a gap between known molecular mechanisms and their clinical manifestations in neurological disorders.

title: Nature's Learning Rule

unexplained_variances: LMS algorithm, traditionally a supervised learning method, can be reformulated to perform unsupervised learning — this contradicts the standard categorization of LMS as inherently requiring an external teaching signal

The claim that Hebbian-LMS may be 'nature's little secret' implies existing pure-Hebbian models of biological learning are incomplete, yet the specific biological evidence for LMS-like error correction at the synapse level is not provided
incidental_findings: The combination of two fundamentally different learning paradigms (unsupervised Hebbian and supervised LMS) yields a new algorithm with 'practical engineering applications' — suggesting cross-paradigm hybrid algorithms may occupy an underexplored design space

The authors imply that living neural networks may use error-minimization (LMS-like) processes even in the absence of explicit supervisory signals, which would reframe unsupervised biological learning as implicitly supervised
technical_sidenotes: The phrase 'learning at the neuron and synapse level' suggests the proposed Hebbian-LMS mechanism operates at individual synaptic junctions rather than at the network or circuit level — a granularity claim that would have significant implications for how local vs. global learning rules are understood in neuroscience

The bridging of signal processing (LMS) and neurobiology (Hebbian) implies there may be a mathematical equivalence or duality between error-driven adaptation and correlation-based plasticity that has not been fully formalized
